candidates.node_relation: Agent identity, access governance, and security control plane for enterprise AI agents and non-human identities.

candidates.theme_relation: If AI agents become embedded in enterprise workflows, identity, permissions, lifecycle management, auditability, and kill-switch controls become prerequisites for scaled deployment.

memory_update.text: Add OKTA as an enterprise AI agent identity/security chokepoint candidate; key thesis is non-human identity governance, permissions, and auditability for agentic workflows.
Add BOX as an unstructured data readiness and content-governance candidate; thesis depends on AI attach rates and whether Intelligent Content Management accelerates revenue growth.
Add VEEV as a vertical enterprise AI software candidate; life-sciences domain context, compliance, and workflow lock-in may create stronger AI monetization than generic copilots.
Add PD as a weaker but relevant AI operations candidate; needs proof that AI-first operations can improve ARR growth and customer retention.
Add DT as an AI observability and runtime intelligence candidate; monitor whether AI-native applications create incremental usage, module adoption, and net retention.

Future Layer 1B passes should separately test data-governance/catalog vendors, low-code workflow vendors, RPA vendors, customer-support automation platforms, SI/consulting implementers, and vertical software outside life sciences.

node: Enterprise AI software, data platforms, security, and automation
summary: Expanded universe for the enterprise AI software/data/automation node, emphasizing second-order chokepoints where enterprise AI adoption may depend on data readiness, workflow embedding, operational resilience, agent identity/security, regulated-domain context, and unstructured-content governance. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation. The strongest current mapping is not simply 'has an AI product,' but 'controls a workflow, data layer, identity layer, or operational control plane that AI agents must access safely and measurably.'
